By Marina Okafor

The first commercial tidal array in the estuary began exporting power on a wet Tuesday, and the harbourmaster logged the event in a hand-written ledger kept since 1911.

Engineers had spent nine years modelling the seabed. The final design used four turbines mounted on a single gravity base, each rated at 1.5 megawatts, and the array feeds a substation built into the old ferry terminal.

## What changed

Two things: blade materials that survive salt water for a decade, and a control system that predicts slack water from a tide table instead of a sensor.

> The economics only work if the machines keep turning through the winter storms.

Local fishermen negotiated a compensation fund, and the array now pauses for six weeks each spring during the smelt run.

## The numbers

| Metric         | Value  |
| -------------- | ------ |
| Capacity       | 6 MW   |
| Annual output  | 21 GWh |
| Homes supplied | 5,400  |

The remaining question is storage: the tide is predictable but not dispatchable, and the battery container on the quay covers only forty minutes of peak demand.
